questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Even after a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not drive until all gates are raised and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is shown on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: Your driver license can be revoked or suspended for:

options.text: Getting 12 or more points on your driving record from traffic violations.
Changing a driver license illegally.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A license can be revoked or suspended for several reasons. These include illegally changing a driver license or getting 12 or more points on your record within 12 months. Drivers under 18 may lose their license if they get 6 or more points within 12 months.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses grip on wet roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a steady speed to get better traction.
Press the brakes hard to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: In heavy rain, even at 30 mph, your tires may float on water instead of gripping the road. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: When an oncoming car has bright headlights at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, only enter an intersection if you can cross it completely before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Give the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. These signs tell drivers that bicycles may be crossing in that area.

questions.question: How can you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Check the inside rearview mirror.
Check the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors. To check your blind spots, look over your shoulders.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
All of them have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They are easier to turn than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than other vehicles at the same speed. A passenger vehicle traveling at 55 mph stops within about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to leave the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther back from the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: When it is hard to see due to darkness or bad weather, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers you may not see.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles
Wherever signs and road markings allow passing
On a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and road markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass at intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleyways. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see ahead. A vehicle might be coming. Only pass where signs and road markings permit it. Make sure you have enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: When changing lanes, how do you check your blind spot?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror
Turn your head and look over your shoulder
Use your side mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all blind spots. Before changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to see these hidden areas.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light will bounce back into your eyes
Oncoming vehicles might not see you
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will bounce back into your eyes
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam light reflects back toward you. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start from which lane?

options.text: Any lane (if it is safe)
The lane closest to the left curb
The center lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, start from the far left lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Motorist services
Construction and maintenance
Distance information to specific locations

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services
questions.explanation: Blue signs provide information about motorist services. These include rest areas, food, gas, and hospitals.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you
You must yield to the pedestrian
Honk your horn to alert them

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to the pedestrian
questions.explanation: A guide dog or white cane means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to them.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the road when safe
Turn back onto the road immediately
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the road when safe
questions.explanation: Do not turn back suddenly. Reduce speed, check traffic, and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing, when do you have enough space to return to your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to re-enter
When you see the passed car behind you over your shoulder
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: You have a safe gap when you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror. Then it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: You see one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line in the center. The broken line is next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot pass in this area
You can pass on the left if no oncoming traffic is present
You can only make right turns here

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left if no oncoming traffic is present
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you are in a passing zone. You can pass if the way is clear.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries or major damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely
Do not move your vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely
questions.explanation: After a minor collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of traffic if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does a single broken white centerline mean?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You can cross it to change lanes.
You can change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross it to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. A broken white line means it is legal to pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before entering the intersection.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light to proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down, check for traffic, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to where you want to go. For a left turn on a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that traffic may merge into their lane from the right.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a collision.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn to avoid collisions. Do not use it to make other drivers go faster or get out of your way.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large commercial vehicle?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for long stretches of time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a pedestrian crosswalk ahead. Be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Decrease your following distance.
Drive through carefully without slowing to look around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through carefully without slowing to look around.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual things in construction zones. This causes traffic problems. Pass through carefully and keep your attention on driving.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for a green light before proceeding.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down, pay attention, and proceed with caution. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.
